extraction.body: Colossal Biosciences just dropped its most ambitious tech play yet - an AI platform designed to fast-track the company's moonshot mission of bringing extinct species back to life. The Dallas-based startup, already valued at $1.5 billion, is betting that artificial intelligence can solve the complex genetic puzzles that have slowed de-extinction research for decades. Peter Diamandis has backed the move with a new fund specifically targeting startups that leverage the platform. The de-extinction game just got its biggest tech upgrade. Colossal Biosciences, the company trying to bring back woolly mammoths and Tasmanian tigers, announced today it's opening up its AI-powered research platform to the broader scientific community - and investors are already lining up. While Colossal has raised over $225 million since 2021, the company's core mission - literally resurrecting extinct species - faces massive technical hurdles that could take decades to overcome. By platformizing its AI tools, the startup is creating a new revenue stream while positioning itself as the infrastructure backbone for next-generation biotech. Peter Diamandis, the XPRIZE founder who's been bullish on longevity and biotech investments, didn't waste time. He's launching a dedicated fund to back startups that build on Colossal's platform, essentially betting that the company's AI tools will spawn an entire ecosystem of genetic engineering applications. The platform leverages machine learning to tackle some of the most complex challenges in genetic engineering - from predicting how ancient DNA sequences might function in modern cellular environments to optimizing CRISPR edits for maximum accuracy. What took Colossal's team months of trial and error can now be modeled and tested virtually before any lab work begins. The AI platform could accelerate research into everything from crop resilience to rare disease treatments. By making these tools available to smaller research teams and startups, Colossal is essentially democratizing access to cutting-edge genetic engineering capabilities that were previously locked behind massive R&D budgets. While companies like Ginkgo Bioworks have built platforms for synthetic biology, Colossal's focus on extinct species has forced them to solve uniquely challenging problems around incomplete genetic data and cellular compatibility. Those solutions now become competitive advantages in the broader biotech market. Diamandis's fund signals that investors see Colossal as more than a science experiment. The company is building the picks and shovels for a new gold rush in genetic engineering, where the real money might not be in the headline-grabbing de-extinction projects but in the infrastructure that makes thousands of smaller innovations possible. For Colossal, the platform launch solves a critical business model question. De-extinction timelines are measured in decades, but platform revenue can start flowing immediately. Every startup that uses their AI tools to design better gene therapies or engineer more resilient crops validates the underlying technology while generating cash flow to fund the moonshot projects. The biotech industry has been waiting for this kind of infrastructure play. Most genetic engineering startups spend years building basic computational tools before they can focus on their core research. Colossal's platform could compress that timeline from years to months, potentially unleashing a wave of innovation across multiple sectors. Colossal Biosciences is making a smart pivot from pure research play to platform provider, creating immediate revenue opportunities while advancing their long-term de-extinction goals. With Diamandis backing the ecosystem play, we're likely seeing the emergence of a new category in biotech infrastructure. The real test will be whether the platform can deliver the promised acceleration in genetic engineering timelines - and whether enough startups adopt it to create the network effects that make platforms truly valuable.

extraction.body: Colossal Biosciences , the world’s first de-extinction company, announced new scientific milestones that will accelerate dodo de-extinction efforts — or bringing back the extinct dodo bird. Building on last year’s advances in pigeon primordial germ cells, gene-edited chicken surrogates and comparative avian genomes, today Colossal unveiled GenoMorph, its AI platform developed to identify potential gene-editing targets from limited genomic data. Applied to the dodo program, the platform identified an estimated 2,300 candidate regulatory elements associated with avian beak size and shape. It’s a pretty ambitious effort, and the company said once before it was making better progress than expected . And the firm has convinced investors to give it hundreds of millions of dollars to develop the science to bring back lost species. There are skeptics, but it is interesting to note that the company has already claimed success in bringing back dire wolves . The company has raised $615 million and it has 270 employees. And previously, Colossal said it had figured out how to make artificial eggs to breed avian species. The artificial egg will be useful for the purpose of hatching eggs, but the company still has to make progress on the genetics behind making new birds. Colossal also announced advances across its avian de-extinction pipeline, including substantially improving the dodo genome assembly through the use of technology from its dire wolf project, an expanded Nicobar pigeon colony, newly derived Nicobar primordial germ cells, chicken embryonic-stem-cell chimeras and a breakthrough lipid-nanoparticle system for gene editing delivery in avian embryos. Together, these capabilities provide the genomic, cellular and reproductive foundation required to translate predicted dodo traits into experimentally validated edits. Colossal has developed GenoMorph, an AI-powered platform that identifies potential gene-editing targets for de-extinction projects with limited genomic data. The platform combines comparative genomics, developmental biology and high-resolution 3D morphology to predict which regulatory elements may be active during development and identifies those most strongly associated with differences in physical form. Unlike protein-coding genes, which provide instructions for building an animal, regulatory DNA controls when, where and how strongly those instructions are activated. These genetic “switches” help shape traits such as the size and structure of a bird’s skull and beak. “De-extinction is as much a data problem as a biology problem,” said Ben Lamm, CEO and cofounder of Colossal, in a statement. “Because so few dodo genomes survive, we cannot rely on the population-level comparisons available for many living species. Our GenoMorph platform provides another path: it learns how regulatory DNA shapes living birds, then identifies the genetic switches that may have contributed to the dodo’s distinctive anatomy. This is more than a solution for the dodo. It provides a repeatable approach for extinct species whose genomic records are similarly limited.” To build GenoMorph, Colossal’s avian team created an avian regulatory atlas using hundreds of samples from chickens, quail, ducks and pigeons. The samples covered six stages of embryonic development and three regions of the developing face. Elements confirmed to influence craniofacial development may then be considered for precision genome editing in the Nicobar pigeon, providing a data-driven path toward reconstructing key aspects of the dodo’s distinctive anatomy. “The dodo’s defining anatomy emerged from networks of regulatory instructions that are difficult to interpret from ancient DNA alone,” said Beth Shapiro, Colossal’s Chief Science Officer, in a statement. “The answer turned out to be comparative: use the breadth of living bird diversity, combined with AI, to identify candidate loci for the next phase of testing. By learning how skulls and beaks develop across living birds, GenoMorph allows us to prioritize the regulatory changes most likely to have shaped the dodo and move them into functional validation. It establishes a repeatable framework for connecting ancient genomes to extinct traits.” “You cannot train AI to answer a precise developmental question using just generic data,” said Anna Keyte, Avian Species Director at Colossal., in a statement “We needed to capture how regulatory activity changes across species, developmental stages and different regions of the face. Building that dataset required more than a year of focused experimental work, and it is what allows GenoMorph to generate biologically meaningful predictions.” Candidate elements are now entering functional-validation studies. Those confirmed to influence craniofacial development may be prioritized for precision editing in the Nicobar pigeon genome. Preliminary findings have been presented at the Craniofacial Gordon Research Conference and the Society for Molecular Biology and Evolution annual conference and the 2026 Society for Molecular Biology and Evolution annual meeting. While this work advances the dodo de-extinction program, its scientific implications extend well beyond a single species. The ability to predict developmentally active regulatory DNA from genome sequence alone, and to validate that against quantitative morphological data across a broad comparative sample, provides a scalable framework for studying the genetic basis of complex anatomical traits in any bird lineage. This includes endangered species for which large population genomic datasets are unlikely ever to exist, where identifying functionally relevant regulatory variants has previously been intractable. The dodo genome assembly that Colossal’s team is using is of extremely high quality for ancient DNA, thanks to the excellent preservation of the dodo specimen from which the genomic data was extracted. However, the fragmented nature of ancient DNA means that, despite this excellent preservation, gaps in the genome sequence remain that can impact analysis. Through the dire wolf program, the company developed a computational genome-assembly method that, applied to improve the dodo genome assembly, demonstrates how technologies created for one de-extinction project can be refined and applied across Colossal’s broader species portfolio. Ancient DNA is fragmented into short strands of surviving DNA, damaged due to degradation, and the genome sequence is often substantially different from that of its closest living relative. Conventional assembly methods map ancient DNA fragments against a living reference genome—in this case, the Nicobar pigeon—and may discard fragments that are too divergent to align. This can leave gaps in the assembly and bias the reconstructed genome toward the living species. Colossal’s published iterative assembly method addresses this limitation by using newly mapped dodo DNA to progressively update the reference genome. The updated reference is then used to map the ancient DNA again, allowing previously unmatched fragments to “walk” into gaps with each successive round. After repeating this process until the number of newly recovered dodo sequences reached a plateau, the result is a substantially more complete assembly than would have been possible through a conventional single-pass approach. Our dodo genome has, for example, 95% of bases covered at least 5-fold (meaning that at least five unique ancient DNA molecules map to more than 95% of letters in the genome), and an average coverage of 65-fold. “We are in the final stages of our analysis of the dodo genome, with much more to come after the genome paper goes through peer review. In the meantime, it’s been rewarding to see that an approach developed for the dire wolf is now producing value across another species program. That repeatability is central to Colossal’s model: every scientific breakthrough becomes part of a scalable technology platform that can accelerate the programs that follow,” said Beth Shapiro. Colossal has expanded its Texas colony of Nicobar pigeons—the dodo’s closest living relative—to 36 birds following successful breeding among established pairs. The growing colony provides an increasingly robust foundation for studying Nicobar pigeon development, reproduction, and genetics while supporting the company’s dodo de-extinction program. Eggs collected during the latest breeding season were used to derive Nicobar pigeon primordial germ cells, or PGCs. These are the cells that eventually develop into sperm and eggs. Establishing these cells is essential to our path of creating heritable genome edits and producing future generations of birds carrying selected dodo traits. Colossal is also working to develop a telomere-to-telomere Nicobar pigeon genome, improving on the existing chromosome-level assembly. This will provide a stronger foundation for identifying potential edits and for improving the genome of the Rodrigues solitaire, an extinct relative of the dodo. Colossal plans to add newly available solitaire sequence data and remap it against the improved Nicobar reference to increase its coverage and completeness. Colossal scientists have also developed a new platform using avian embryonic stem cells to generate chimeric chickens, and have successfully hatched the first chimeras produced through the platform. Embryonic stem cells offer a route to introduce engineered cells into a developing embryo and observe how those cells contribute to the phenotype of the bird. Hatching viable chimeric chickens confirms that the cultured cells retain the developmental potential needed to integrate into a host embryo and contribute to its various tissues. Colossal is also expanding their embryonic stem cell culture system to pigeons to support the dodo de-extinction program. By editing embryonic stem cells and using these edited cells to create chimeric pigeons, scientists can test whether the edits have the predicted effect on phenotype before editing PGCs. This establishes a platform for phenotype screening, allowing the team to test candidate edits and evaluate their effects before combining them on the path to a dodo. In another world’s first, Colossal has also developed a lipid-nanoparticle delivery platform that efficiently introduces DNA, RNA, and CRISPR gene-editing tools into developing bird embryos while improving embryo viability over traditional delivery methods. In experiments, editing the bone-development regulator Runx2 produced a clear craniofacial phenotype, demonstrating the platform’s ability to test how specific genetic changes affect avian development. The system has also been used successfully in rock dove and duck embryos, supporting its application across bird species. Colossal scientists are now using the lipid-nanoparticle delivery platform to validate regulatory elements identified by GenoMorph in near real time. The strongest candidates are being engineered into Nicobar pigeon primordial germ cells for further precision-editing studies. Colossal’s dodo de-extinction update focuses primarily on a new AI platform called GenoMorph. In conjunction with this announcement, the avian team is post a new paper to bioRxiv about an innovation in gene-editing tool delivery. The team developed a lipid-nanoparticle delivery method that allows us to use gene-editing tools on developing bird embryos, and we proved that it worked across three different avian species. GenoMorph is an internal AI platform that identifies gene-editing targets in genomic data. The tool uses comparative genomics, developmental biology, and high-resolution 3D morphology to help us understand which genes are important to the development of physical features like the shape of a beak or the size of a skull. “To recreate the dodo’s iconic beak size and skull shape, we can’t just write instructions for a final outcome. We need to build the instructions for how to get there,” the company said. “So we’re studying beak development across a range of different bird species, and we’re using AI to identify which regulatory elements to target. So far, GenoMorph has identified 653 candidate regulatory elements associated with beak size, and 1,698 associated with beak thickness and breadth. In over a billion base pairs of DNA, that’s major progress for narrowing our search.” But this isn’t just about software. This announcement is full of updates about dodo de-extinction. Colossal is making major progress on the de-extinction of the dodo. Colossal said it has decoded more of the dodo’s genome, and it has a growing colony of its closest living relative, and we’ve been able to derive critically important cells that will one day help us hatch dodos. The method usited to assemble the dire wolf genome, published in Cell this year, helped the company generate a substantially more complete dodo genome than ever. And its colony of Nicobar pigeons, the dodo’s closest living relative, is growing and thriving. The firm has successfully hatched chicken chimeras using avian embryonic stem cells, helping us confirm that our genetic edits result in the changes it wants.

So far, GenoMorph has identified 653 candidate regulatory elements associated with beak size, and 1,698 associated with beak thickness and breadth. In over a billion base pairs of DNA, that’s major progress for narrowing our search.”
But this isn’t just about software. This announcement is full of updates about dodo de-extinction. Colossal is making major progress on the de-extinction of the dodo.

Colossal said it has decoded more of the dodo’s genome, and it has a growing colony of its closest living relative, and we’ve been able to derive critically important cells that will one day help us hatch dodos.
The method usited to assemble the dire wolf genome, published in Cell this year, helped the company generate a substantially more complete dodo genome than ever.

And its colony of Nicobar pigeons, the dodo’s closest living relative, is growing and thriving. The firm has successfully hatched chicken chimeras using avian embryonic stem cells, helping us confirm that our genetic edits result in the changes it wants.

passages: NEW YORK , Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Platinum Trade Alerts (PTA) News Commentary - Advanced AI, real-time battlefield intelligence and autonomous coordination are reshaping the future of defense operations as global investment accelerates. - Artificial intelligence is changing the way military operations are planned, managed and carried out. As defense forces deploy more drones, unmanned ground vehicles, surveillance systems and connected sensors, the ability to make sense of all that information is becoming just as important as the hardware itself. That is where Autonomous Mission Intelligence comes in. By combining AI, real-time data analysis, machine vision and automated mission planning, these technologies can help military personnel understand what is happening on the ground, identify potential threats and coordinate multiple systems more effectively. The market is already attracting significant attention. Grand View Research valued the global artificial intelligence in military market at approximately $9.3 billion in 2024 and projects it will reach $19.3 billion by 2030. For defense technology companies, that growth points to a larger opportunity as governments look for ways to process intelligence faster, improve battlefield awareness and make better-informed decisions when time is critical. Companies leading the Autonomous and AI technology Defense Operations boom include: VisionWave Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: VWAV ), BigBear.ai (NYSE: BBAI ), Palladyne AI Corp. (NASDAQ: PDYN ), AIRO Group Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: AIRO ), MicroVision, Inc. (NASDAQ: MVIS ).

The opportunity extends well beyond traditional military AI software. As autonomous aircraft, robotic platforms and networked defense systems become more sophisticated, mission intelligence is positioned to become the software layer connecting these technologies, helping them interpret changing conditions, prioritize information and coordinate activities with appropriate human oversight. The Business Research Company estimates that the global AI in aerospace and defense market will grow from $29.27 billion in 2025 to $55.3 billion by 2030, representing a projected compound annual growth rate of 13.5%. Meanwhile, its AI-powered autonomous defense system market forecast projects growth from $13.77 billion in 2025 to $34.02 billion by 2030, a 19.9% annual growth rate. These are broader markets rather than standalone valuations for Autonomous Mission Intelligence, but they highlight the scale of investment flowing toward intelligent, connected and increasingly autonomous defense capabilities. Companies developing mission-planning software, edge AI, sensor integration, autonomous coordination and real-time decision-support technologies could be positioned to compete for a growing share of this spending.
Five Key Drivers of the Autonomous Mission Intelligence Opportunity:

VisionWave (NASDAQ: VWAV ) Advances Stratum AI, an Agentic AI Architecture for Autonomous Mission Intelligence and Orchestration - VisionWave Holdings Inc. ("VisionWave" or the "Company") today highlighted the development of Stratum AI, the Company's agentic artificial intelligence ("AI") mission-intelligence and orchestration layer, which is under development and is designed to connect autonomous platforms, sensors and mission workflows across defense, homeland security and commercial applications.
Developing Intelligence Layer Is Designed to Coordinate Autonomous Systems, AI Agents, Sensor Fusion and Mission Workflows Across Air and Ground
Stratum AI is being developed alongside STRATUM Command, a further AI-enabled sensing, mission-intelligence and situational-awareness capability that is likewise under development.

Together, the technologies are intended to coordinate autonomous systems, AI agents and mission workflows while fusing field information and delivering real-time decision support. These capabilities are under development. Neither Stratum AI nor STRATUM Command is commercially available, neither has generated revenue, and the Company has not completed independent third-party testing or validation of either.
Other recent developments in the autonomous, AI industries of note include:

BigBear.ai (NYSE: BBAI ), a specialized security and defense technology company providing mission-ready AI, announced it has secured more than $225 million in contract awards since July across homeland security, defense, intelligence and federal civilian customers. The awards represent both new wins and successful recompetes in the core of BigBear.ai's business, which is focused on expanding in the National Security and Trade & Travel markets.

"Retaining critical work with CBP while adding the FBI, the Coast Guard and new defense and intelligence customers is proof of a strong foundation and an expanding customer base," said Kevin McAleenan, CEO of BigBear.ai. "Technology does not translate into capability without operational insight, and these awards come from customers who understand both the depth of our experience and our differentiated technology."

As part of these wins, BigBear.ai won more than 25 new generative AI awards across federal agencies, including the FBI, NASA, the U.S. Coast Guard, the Department of Energy and the Department of Veterans Affairs. SwarmShot will combine Federal's specialized counter-UAS shotshell ammunition, a lightweight Mossberg weapon module purpose-engineered for airborne operation, and Palladyne AI's IntelliSwarm™ autonomy system, which combines BRAIN avionics with SwarmOS™ collaborative autonomy software.

The system will initially be developed as a modular mission add-on for Gremlin-X™, Palladyne AI's Group 1 quadcopter mini-bomber. The lightweight architecture is designed to support reliable operation across a wide range of environmental conditions while helping mitigate thermal runaway propagation to enhance overall system safety.

"We are pleased to partner with Calogy Solutions as we advance the development of our next-generation hybrid-electric VTOL platform," said Eric Côté, President, Jaunt Air Mobility Canada. "Their expertise in battery engineering and their innovative thermal management technology align well with our focus on building a safe, reliable and high-performance aircraft capable of operating in demanding environments. We look forward to working together as we move the program toward flight testing and commercialization."

The integrated capability has potential applications across commercial, civil, public safety and global defense markets where rapidly changing conditions can make timely situational awareness and actionable data critical.

( $VWAV ) ("VisionWave" or the "Company") a defense technology company focused on autonomous systems, advanced sensing, artificial intelligence, and battlefield autonomy, today announced the unveiling of its TALON™ Tactical Autonomous Aerial System and D-FLY™ Autonomous Intercept Platform at Eurosatory 2026, one of the world's largest and most influential defense and security exhibitions. The unveiling marks an important step in VisionWave's ongoing development of integrated, operational autonomous defense solutions. The systems were physically showcased alongside other VisionWave technologies, demonstrating the Company's growing ability to field interoperable autonomous platforms designed for modern military, homeland security, border security, and critical infrastructure protection missions. Developed through VisionWave UK Ltd. and manufactured in England in cooperation with specialized aerospace and defense partners, TALON™ and D-FLY™ represent the latest additions to VisionWave's expanding STRATUM™ autonomous operations architecture. "Eurosatory 2026 represented an important mile stone for VisionWave," said Douglas Davis, Executive Chairman of VisionWave Holdings. "For the first time, we publicly demonstrated multiple autonomous platforms operating within a common ecosystem. TALON™, D-FLY™, VARAN™ and CAEAN™ collectively showcase VisionWave's ability to integrate artificial intelligence, sensing, autonomy, communications, mission intelligence and operational execution into deployable defense solutions. These represent advanced systems designed for demanding operational environments." TALON™ - Tactical Autonomous Aerial System - TALON™ is a high-performance tactical autonomous aerial platform intended to support intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance (ISR), communications relay, distributed sensing, payload delivery and persistent battlefield overwatch missions. Designed for contested and degraded environments, TALON™ is intended to enables operators to extend situational awareness and operational reach while reducing risk to personnel. D-FLY™ - Autonomous Counter-UAS Intercept Platform - D-FLY™ is a rapid-response autonomous aerial interceptor designed specifically to address the growing global threat posed by hostile drones and low-altitude unmanned aerial systems. Designed for tactical airspace protection, D-FLY™ is intended to provide security forces and military operators with a highly mobile autonomous solution for detecting, tracking and responding to emerging aerial threats. (NYSE American: UMAC) , a domestic manufacturer of NDAA-compliant drone components. Powerus previously announced a proposed merger with Aureus Greenway Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: PUSA ). The investment strengthens a working relationship already in place between the two companies, under which Powerus sources drone components and hardware from Unusual Machines. The companies' interests are closely aligned: as Powerus scales its production of autonomous and counter-drone systems, it has been and expects to be a meaningful customer for U.S.-made components of the kind Unusual Machines supplies. Powerus is under no obligation to purchase any specific volume of parts, and the two companies operate independently; the relationship reflects a shared focus on building a domestic, U.S.-based defense-autonomy supply chain. "Unusual Machines has been a valued partner as we've scaled, and this investment reflects the strength of that relationship and our shared commitment to American-made autonomy," said Andrew Fox, CEO of Powerus. "The more we grow, the more we both benefit from a resilient domestic supply chain." Ondas Inc. (NASDAQ: ONDS ), a leading provider of autonomous drone and advanced defense technologies, announced that it has secured more than $40 million in aggregate new orders during June for autonomous defense systems, including Counter-UAS ("C-UAS") solutions, Loitering Munition Systems ("LMS"), ground systems and related defense services from governmental and defense customers across multiple international markets. Together with previously announced awards, these new orders bring Ondas' second-quarter-to-date order activity to more than $150 million. The new awards reflect continued demand for Ondas' autonomous defense technologies as governments and defense forces respond to rapidly evolving threats from unmanned aerial systems, and a growing demand for long-range precision strike platforms. Ondas believes the growth of the LMS market represents a natural extension of the same operational forces driving demand for C-UAS technologies. Red Cat Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: RCAT) , a U.S.-based provider of advanced all-domain drone and robotic solutions for defense and national security, recently introduced Hellcat™, a dual-use small unmanned aircraft system (sUAS) built on the proven Black Widow™ platform and designed for rapidly evolving operational environments. Red Cat is unveiling Hellcat in conjunction with Eurosatory 2026, where defense leaders, government buyers, and industry partners from across Europe and allied nations are convening to evaluate current and future capabilities with a focus on small UAS, contested-environment operations, and interoperable systems. Built on the proven Black Widow platform, Hellcat incorporates extensive feedback gathered directly from warfighters in the field and lessons learned through an ongoing partnership with Ukraine. extraction.body: October 14, 2026 08:50 ET | Source: FN Media FN Media NEW YORK, Oct. 14, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Artificial intelligence is changing the way military operations are planned, managed and carried out. As defense forces deploy more drones, unmanned ground vehicles, surveillance systems and connected sensors, the ability to make sense of all that information is becoming just as important as the hardware itself. That is where Autonomous Mission Intelligence comes in. By combining AI, real-time data analysis, machine vision and automated mission planning, these technologies can help military personnel understand what is happening on the ground, identify potential threats and coordinate multiple systems more effectively. The market is already attracting significant attention. Grand View Research valued the global artificial intelligence in military market at approximately $9.3 billion in 2024 and projects it will reach $19.3 billion by 2030. For defense technology companies, that growth points to a larger opportunity as governments look for ways to process intelligence faster, improve battlefield awareness and make better-informed decisions when time is critical. Companies leading the Autonomous and AI technology Defense Operations boom include: VisionWave Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: VWAV), Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: KTOS), Ondas Inc. (NASDAQ: ONDS), AeroVironment, Inc. (NASDAQ: AVAV), UiPath, Inc. (NYSE: PATH). The opportunity extends well beyond traditional military AI software. As autonomous aircraft, robotic platforms and networked defense systems become more sophisticated, mission intelligence is positioned to become the software layer connecting these technologies, helping them interpret changing conditions, prioritize information and coordinate activities with appropriate human oversight. The Business Research Company estimates that the global AI in aerospace and defense market will grow from $29.27 billion in 2025 to $55.3 billion by 2030, representing a projected compound annual growth rate of 13.5%. Meanwhile, its AI-powered autonomous defense system market forecast projects growth from $13.77 billion in 2025 to $34.02 billion by 2030, a 19.9% annual growth rate. These are broader markets rather than standalone valuations for Autonomous Mission Intelligence, but they highlight the scale of investment flowing toward intelligent, connected and increasingly autonomous defense capabilities. Companies developing mission-planning software, edge AI, sensor integration, autonomous coordination and real-time decision-support technologies could be positioned to compete for a growing share of this spending. Five Key Drivers of the Autonomous Mission Intelligence Opportunity: VisionWave (NASDAQ: VWAV) Advances Stratum AI, an Agentic AI Architecture for Autonomous Mission Intelligence and Orchestration - VisionWave Holdings Inc. (“VisionWave” or the “Company”) today highlighted the development of Stratum AI, the Company’s agentic artificial intelligence (“AI”) mission-intelligence and orchestration layer, which is under development and is designed to connect autonomous platforms, sensors and mission workflows across defense, homeland security and commercial applications. Developing Intelligence Layer Is Designed to Coordinate Autonomous Systems, AI Agents, Sensor Fusion and Mission Workflows Across Air and Ground Stratum AI is being developed alongside STRATUM Command, a further AI-enabled sensing, mission-intelligence and situational-awareness capability that is likewise under development. Together, the technologies are intended to coordinate autonomous systems, AI agents and mission workflows while fusing field information and delivering real-time decision support. These capabilities are under development. Neither Stratum AI nor STRATUM Command is commercially available, neither has generated revenue, and the Company has not completed independent third-party testing or validation of either. “Autonomy is ultimately an intelligence problem, not simply a vehicle problem,” said Douglas Davis, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of VisionWave. “We believe a drone, ground vehicle or sensor can be more useful when it can contribute to—and act upon—a common operational picture. Stratum AI is being developed as the intelligence and orchestration layer connecting that ecosystem.” Agentic AI Mission Orchestration - VisionWave is designing the architecture around three principal functions: Other recent developments in the autonomous, AI, defense industries of note include: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: KTOS), a technology company in defense, national security, and global markets, announced major advancements in its turbojet technology. Highlighting these achievements are the recent successful flight tests of the TDI-J85 (J85) engine across multiple configurations, including Lugged Launch, Palletized, and Surface-to-Surface applications. “Our successful flight tests across diverse deployment methods prove the versatility and reliability of the TDI-J85 engine,” said Joseph Kovasity, Senior Vice President of Kratos TDI. “By pairing this operational success with a fully functional, high-rate manufacturing capability, we are transforming how the industry approaches affordable propulsion. Kratos’ recent 3,000-engine component order for 2027 production and our path to 10,000+ engines annually by 2029 demonstrate our commitment to delivering mass and capability to the warfighter at an unprecedented scale.” Ondas Inc. (Nasdaq: ONDS), a leading provider of advanced autonomous systems and next-generation defense and security technologies and service, announced the successful completion of the installation and European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) certification of its advanced Airborne Missile Protection System (AMPS), incorporating Directional Infrared Countermeasures (DIRCM), on a Bombardier Global 7500 aircraft. The certification marks an important milestone in Ondas' expansion into the global airborne defense and aircraft protection market, adding another high-value VVIP aircraft platform to the growing range of aircraft protected by the Company's advanced missile protection technologies. The achievement demonstrates Ondas' capabilities in delivering complex, fully integrated protection systems that meet stringent international aviation certification requirements. AeroVironment, Inc. (NASDAQ: AVAV) and NIOA Australia have signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to explore opportunities to expand Australian industry participation supporting AV’s one-way attack systems. Signed during LAND FORCES 2026, the agreement establishes a framework for AV and NIOA to identify and facilitate a path forward for the localization, co-production and sustainment of AV’s one-way attack systems in Australia. Under the MOU, the companies will explore opportunities to combine AV’s autonomous systems with NIOA’s sovereign weapons and munitions expertise. Potential areas of cooperation include local manufacturing and integration, in-country support and sustainment, and the development of Australian variants incorporating NIOA-developed payloads, warheads and mission effects where technically, commercially and legally feasible. UiPath, Inc. (NYSE: PATH), a leader in business orchestration and automation, recently announced it has been recognized as a Leader in the Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Agentic Software Quality Assurance Platforms. A complimentary copy of this research report is available here . As enterprises move beyond experimenting with agentic testing, the challenge is turning its potential into something that works in production: across real applications, deployment environments and release cycles, with the security, governance and reliability enterprises require. passages: Ricursive Intelligence founders Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini believe more efficient AI chip design could help solve the compute crisis.

The founders took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Wednesday to detail how their startup is developing AI that can design chips, learn from each iteration, and improve subsequent designs, all with the goal of automating and accelerating the chip design process.

We think that we need to help by making chips that are more efficient, that use the bandwidth in those data centers more efficiently, that use the wafers and fabs more efficiently, because even if we make [data centers] in space or something, I don’t know, you won’t see the sun anymore.”
The founders also argued that AI-designed chips will make it possible to create all sorts of chips that might not have been possible before.

While some may be scared by the thought of AI designing its own chips, Goldie argues that letting AI handle chip design will allow humans can focus on developing applications and exploring new possibilities that can expand what they can accomplish with computing.

The founders took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Wednesday to detail how their startup is developing AI that can design chips, learn from each iteration, and improve subsequent designs, all with the goal of automating and accelerating the chip design process. “There is this understanding that in the next five years we are going to have at least 10,000x more demand for compute, and that’s somewhat potentially conservative,” Goldie said on stage. “So we don’t want to build 10,000 times more data centers. We think that we need to help by making chips that are more efficient, that use the bandwidth in those data centers more efficiently, that use the wafers and fabs more efficiently, because even if we make [data centers] in space or something, I don’t know, you won’t see the sun anymore.” While some may be scared by the thought of AI designing its own chips, Goldie argues that letting AI handle chip design will allow humans can focus on developing applications and exploring new possibilities that can expand what they can accomplish with computing. “I think the way everything is shifting is that humans come bring their great ideas and creative thoughts, and execution is handled by AI,” Goldie said. “And this is happening in chip design, software development, and other places. And that’s something that recursive does for chip design.” The founders say AI is challenging traditional chip design methods by discovering unconventional layouts that can outperform traditional ones. For example, AlphaChip, the AI system the founders previously developed, produced a circular, “donut-shaped” arrangement of chip components that initially surprised engineers but ultimately proved to be successful. They explained that they are optimizing entire chips rather than following the traditional approach of partitioning them into dozens of smaller blocks. This approach allows AI to create intricate patterns, including wave-like designs, which the pair said they plan to share more about in the future. sources.title: Ricursive Intelligence Bets AI Can Solve Chip Design Crisis
passages: Ricursive Intelligence emerged from stealth today with a platform that promises to automate the notoriously complex chip design process, using machine learning to iterate and improve with each design cycle.
The real test will be whether AI can match the precision and creativity that human engineers have brought to chip design for decades.
Traditional chip design requires teams of engineers working through countless iterations, debugging complex architectures, and optimizing for performance metrics.
Chip design involves balancing countless variables - power consumption, heat generation, processing speed, manufacturing constraints, and cost optimization.

Just as Google Cloud's Gemini Agent has been automating enterprise workflows and Meta's Muse platform has been streamlining small business operations, Ricursive is applying similar principles to semiconductor design.
While most solutions focus on manufacturing capacity, Ricursive is betting that the real bottleneck is in the design phase itself.

The company's approach tackles one of the industry's most persistent problems - the months or even years it takes to design and validate new semiconductors. Traditional chip design requires teams of engineers working through countless iterations, debugging complex architectures, and optimizing for performance metrics. The global chip shortage has exposed just how brittle our semiconductor supply chains really are, with everything from cars to gaming consoles sitting idle in factories waiting for processors. The founders took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Wednesday to detail how their startup is developing AI that can design chips, learn from each iteration, and improve subsequent designs, all with the goal of automating and accelerating the chip design process. “There is this understanding that in the next five years we are going to have at least 10,000x more demand for compute, and that’s somewhat potentially conservative,” Goldie said on stage. “So we don’t want to build 10,000 times more data centers. We think that we need to help by making chips that are more efficient, that use the bandwidth in those data centers more efficiently, that use the wafers and fabs more efficiently, because even if we make [data centers] in space or something, I don’t know, you won’t see the sun anymore.” While some may be scared by the thought of AI designing its own chips, Goldie argues that letting AI handle chip design will allow humans can focus on developing applications and exploring new possibilities that can expand what they can accomplish with computing. “I think the way everything is shifting is that humans come bring their great ideas and creative thoughts, and execution is handled by AI,” Goldie said. “And this is happening in chip design, software development, and other places. And that’s something that recursive does for chip design.” The founders say AI is challenging traditional chip design methods by discovering unconventional layouts that can outperform traditional ones. For example, AlphaChip, the AI system the founders previously developed, produced a circular, “donut-shaped” arrangement of chip components that initially surprised engineers but ultimately proved to be successful. They explained that they are optimizing entire chips rather than following the traditional approach of partitioning them into dozens of smaller blocks. This approach allows AI to create intricate patterns, including wave-like designs, which the pair said they plan to share more about in the future. extraction.body: Ricursive Intelligence founders Anna Goldie and Azalia Mirhoseini believe more efficient AI chip design could help solve the compute crisis. The founders took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt on Wednesday to detail how their startup is developing AI that can design chips, learn from each iteration, and improve subsequent designs, all with the goal of automating and accelerating the chip design process. “There is this understanding that in the next five years we are going to have at least 10,000x more demand for compute, and that’s somewhat potentially conservative,” Goldie said on stage. “So we don’t want to build 10,000 times more data centers. We think that we need to help by making chips that are more efficient, that use the bandwidth in those data centers more efficiently, that use the wafers and fabs more efficiently, because even if we make [data centers] in space or something, I don’t know, you won’t see the sun anymore.” While some may be scared by the thought of AI designing its own chips, Goldie argues that letting AI handle chip design will allow humans can focus on developing applications and exploring new possibilities that can expand what they can accomplish with computing. “I think the way everything is shifting is that humans come bring their great ideas and creative thoughts, and execution is handled by AI,” Goldie said. “And this is happening in chip design, software development, and other places. And that’s something that recursive does for chip design.” The founders say AI is challenging traditional chip design methods by discovering unconventional layouts that can outperform traditional ones. For example, AlphaChip, the AI system the founders previously developed, produced a circular, “donut-shaped” arrangement of chip components that initially surprised engineers but ultimately proved to be successful. They explained that they are optimizing entire chips rather than following the traditional approach of partitioning them into dozens of smaller blocks. This approach allows AI to create intricate patterns, including wave-like designs, which the pair said they plan to share more about in the future. The founders also argued that AI-designed chips will make it possible to create all sorts of chips that might not have been possible before. “If it takes six months or a year or two years to design a new chip, then you really have to be extremely selective about the chips that you design,” Goldie said. “But if you can design a chip in like a week, and then say for manufacturing, you can design custom chips for all sorts of different types of applications in like space and AR, VR, and you biological computing, and it makes sense financially to do that, and we can be more energy efficient.” Aisha is a consumer news reporter at TechCrunch. For example, AlphaChip, the AI system the founders previously developed, produced a circular, “donut-shaped” arrangement of chip components that initially surprised engineers but ultimately proved to be successful. extraction.body: A new startup is taking aim at the semiconductor industry's biggest bottleneck with an audacious proposition: let AI design the chips themselves. Ricursive Intelligence emerged from stealth today with a platform that promises to automate the notoriously complex chip design process, using machine learning to iterate and improve with each design cycle. The timing couldn't be more critical as the industry grapples with a compute crisis that's throttling everything from data centers to consumer devices. The semiconductor shortage that's been choking tech supply chains for years just got a potential lifeline from an unexpected source: artificial intelligence. Ricursive Intelligence, a startup that's been quietly developing in stealth mode, just unveiled an AI platform designed to revolutionize how chips are created by letting machines handle the entire design process. The company's approach tackles one of the industry's most persistent problems - the months or even years it takes to design and validate new semiconductors. Traditional chip design requires teams of engineers working through countless iterations, debugging complex architectures, and optimizing for performance metrics. Ricursive's AI platform promises to compress these timelines by learning from each design iteration and automatically improving subsequent attempts. The global chip shortage has exposed just how brittle our semiconductor supply chains really are, with everything from cars to gaming consoles sitting idle in factories waiting for processors. While most solutions focus on manufacturing capacity, Ricursive is betting that the real bottleneck is in the design phase itself. The startup's founders detailed how their platform works during the launch, explaining that their AI doesn't just automate existing design processes - it fundamentally reimagines them. The system analyzes successful chip architectures, identifies patterns in performance optimization, and then applies those learnings to generate entirely new designs. Each iteration feeds back into the system, creating what they describe as a "recursive intelligence" loop that gets smarter with every chip it creates. Just as Google Cloud's Gemini Agent has been automating enterprise workflows and Meta's Muse platform has been streamlining small business operations, Ricursive is applying similar principles to semiconductor design. Chip design involves balancing countless variables - power consumption, heat generation, processing speed, manufacturing constraints, and cost optimization. That's why the industry has been so conservative about embracing automation, preferring human expertise over algorithmic decision-making. But Ricursive's bet is that AI has finally reached the sophistication needed to handle this complexity. Their platform reportedly uses advanced machine learning models trained on decades of chip design data, combined with real-time feedback loops that let the system learn from both successes and failures. The goal isn't to replace human designers entirely, but to accelerate the iteration cycles that currently bottleneck the entire process. The startup joins a growing wave of companies applying AI to traditionally manual processes. We've seen similar approaches in supply chain automation, where former Tesla engineers recently raised $12.5 million to automate logistics operations. The pattern suggests we're entering a phase where AI is moving beyond consumer applications into the foundational infrastructure that powers our digital economy. Major players like Nvidia, AMD, and Intel are all racing to develop more powerful chips for AI workloads, while the broader market struggles with supply constraints that have persisted since the pandemic. If Ricursive's approach proves viable, it could help address both challenges simultaneously - accelerating the development of next-generation processors while reducing the time-to-market that's been hampering supply chain recovery. The company hasn't disclosed funding details or customer partnerships yet, but the launch signals growing confidence in AI's ability to tackle increasingly complex engineering challenges. Whether their approach can deliver on its ambitious promises remains to be seen, but the semiconductor industry's desperate need for faster design cycles suggests there's significant appetite for any solution that can compress development timelines. Ricursive Intelligence's AI-powered chip design platform represents a bold bet on automation solving one of tech's most persistent bottlenecks. While the semiconductor industry has traditionally been conservative about embracing algorithmic design, the ongoing compute crisis and supply chain constraints create unprecedented pressure for innovation. If successful, this approach could fundamentally reshape how chips are developed, potentially accelerating the next generation of processors that power everything from smartphones to data centers. The real test will be whether AI can match the precision and creativity that human engineers have brought to chip design for decades.

passages: Microsoft says it has dismantled a criminal marketplace responsible for 1 billion malicious messages.

“What appears to be a simple scam message is often the visible end of a much larger transnational cybercriminal operation.” The evolving PhaaS marketplace Collectively, YAM Store and the kits and tools sold within it enabled the sending of more than 1 billion messages to 75,000-plus organizations worldwide.

“Working together, and with the assistance of AI tools, we connected accounts, websites, and infrastructure that initially appeared unrelated, helping expose the broader criminal marketplace behind them,” Steven Masada, associate general counsel and GM for Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit, wrote in a blog post.
Investigation into the marketplace began in late 2025 after Japan’s National Police Agency (NPA) notified Microsoft of “a wave of fraud and scam activity” targeting people and businesses in Japan.

Working with international authorities and several tech and cybersecurity companies in a nearly year-long investigation, Redmond identified and took down Yam Store, a coordinated underground network dealing in commercial phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS).
Microsoft said the takedown began as a simple investigation based on a tip from Japanese authorities.
More than 750 million of those were sent to Microsoft customers alone, and ultimately generated “tens of millions of dollars” for criminal operators.

Masada noted that many “used the appearance of official authority to pressure victims into making payments or disclosing sensitive personal information. They advised that users have a basic understanding of common phishing techniques and should be educated to always verify with the purported sender before clicking a link supposedly taking them to a login page, even when the task involves signing in to a known, secure account. These steps can help lock down global administrator roles in particular. They also advised additional actions including the use of the Microsoft Authenticator app for passkeys and MFA; configuration of the Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Safe Links policy to apply to internal recipients; complementing MFA with conditional access policies; and only allowing MFA and passkey registrations from trusted locations and devices.

extraction.body: We’ve all gotten a scam text about a nonexistent parking ticket or a fake package delivery, but hopefully you’ll start seeing fewer of them. These messages have been used to target consumers, healthcare organizations, financial institutions, and other businesses in more than 150 countries, generating tens of millions of dollars for their operators. According to Microsoft’s report, scammers could buy stolen or fraudulent Microsoft and Google accounts on YAM Store and use the phishing kits to send scam messages. Microsoft says YAM Store also hijacked real organizations’ expired web domains and created websites for nonexistent organizations, which it used to get Microsoft accounts it could resell. The Iron Man platform was also offering over 2,300 templates scammers could use to impersonate organizations like banks and police departments. Microsoft says it disabled over 20,000 accounts connected to YAM Store and blocked over 100,000 web domains being used for impersonation and fraud. With health sector cybersecurity non-profit Health-ISAC, Microsoft also seized and redirected web domains that were powering all three platforms.

sources.title: Hirudo Android malware replaces banking apps to evade security checks - BleepingComputer
passages: A new Android malware called Hirudo steals bank account credentials by replacing legitimate banking apps with modified versions that disable security checks.

According to the researchers, “Hirudo marks a deliberate escalation in how Android bankers approach hardened applications,” shifting the focus from device-level integrity checks to the security mechanisms built into banking apps.

ThreatFabric found that Hirudo currently targets Indonesian banking apps and found thousands of application-credential entries in an unsecured backend panel, along with device, lock-screen, and financial-profile data.

A report today from mobile security company ThreatFabric notes that Hirudo has been observed impersonating at least seven Indonesian banks, but the malware also targets financial organizations in China, India, Mexico, Morocco, and Thailand.
The researchers say that these apps act as malware loaders for Hirudo, showing a fake “update” notification that leads to permission-granting prompts, including for Accessibility services
New RemControl Android banking malware targets users in Europe and Canada
New Manic Android malware can exfiltrate data through nearby devices
Once installed, Hirudo launches the real banking app’s uninstaller, downloads a patched copy, and abuses its Accessibility permission to install it.
The malware is typically delivered via apps for shopping (Shopora), adult content (1V1 X), or short drama (ZoyaTV, KoiShort) that appear legitimate and provide the promised functionality.
Once active on the device, Hirudo can steal banking passwords, payment PINs, device-unlock secrets, and SMS messages, stream the screen to operators, and provide access to both cameras.
Low-cost Android phones ship with residential proxy malware

extraction.body: How to remove a Trojan, Virus, Worm, or other Malware A new Android malware called Hirudo steals bank account credentials by replacing legitimate banking apps with modified versions that disable security checks. Researchers identified malicious copies of eight banking apps that use a hooking engine to bypass app-signature, Accessibility, and Play Integrity checks by substituting certificate information or returning empty lists. Threat actors can use Hirudo to steal credentials, remotely control infected phones in real time, collect messages, capture screenshots, and record audio. A report today from mobile security company ThreatFabric notes that Hirudo has been observed impersonating at least seven Indonesian banks, but the malware also targets financial organizations in China, India, Mexico, Morocco, and Thailand. The malware is typically delivered via apps for shopping (Shopora), adult content (1V1 X), or short drama (ZoyaTV, KoiShort) that appear legitimate and provide the promised functionality. The researchers say that these apps act as malware loaders for Hirudo, showing a fake “update” notification that leads to permission-granting prompts, including for Accessibility services Once installed, Hirudo launches the real banking app’s uninstaller, downloads a patched copy, and abuses its Accessibility permission to install it. ThreatFabric explains that this is a delicate, risky process for the malware, since the victim can interrupt it at two points. ThreatFabric found that the malicious copy of a banking app retains almost all of the original app’s code, but loads a hooking engine built on the open-source frameworks YAHFA and Dobby. When launched, the patched app performs the following evasion actions: “With the engine running inside the banking app's own process, the app's defenses are turned against it,” the researchers say . However, ThreatFabric explains there are certain limitations to these evasion methods. The bundled attestation keybox has been publicly leaked, and Google lists two of its certificates as compromised, so server-side revocation checks can detect those forgeries. Once active on the device, Hirudo can steal banking passwords, payment PINs, device-unlock secrets, and SMS messages, stream the screen to operators, and provide access to both cameras. The malware’s fake checkout pages collect payment PINs, then display a fabricated payment-success result to deceive victims while it steals data. ThreatFabric found that Hirudo currently targets Indonesian banking apps and found thousands of application-credential entries in an unsecured backend panel, along with device, lock-screen, and financial-profile data. However, the victim count remains unknown. According to the researchers, “Hirudo marks a deliberate escalation in how Android bankers approach hardened applications,” shifting the focus from device-level integrity checks to the security mechanisms built into banking apps. The researchers suggest that banks should validate integrity and attestation server-side, bind checks to sessions and protected actions, and retain behavioral and transaction-risk controls. Android users are strongly recommended to keep their devices up-to-date, avoid installing APK files sourced from unofficial Android stores, and periodically run Play Protect scans. sources.title: Hirudo Android Trojan Uses Patched Banking Apps to Bypass Their Built-In Security Checks - The Hacker News
passages: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a new Android banking trojan called Hirudo that works by replacing legitimate banking apps with purpose-built patched versions designed to bypass security checks from inside the app itself, marking a new escalation in financial fraud.
While all this behavior is par for the course when it comes to Android banking trojans, it's their attempts to replace the target banking app with a tampered copy that stand out.
"Hirudo marks a deliberate escalation in how Android bankers approach hardened applications," ThreatFabric said.

"By moving its tampering inside the target app, the operation shifts the contest from the device to the application's own integrity checks, and from a bespoke patch to a reusable engine that can be retargeted at other apps and regions."

"The operation combines credential theft, device takeover, screen and camera capture, and SMS theft, in combination with a fairly mature backend," Eward Driehuis, vice president of fraud engineering at ThreatFabric, said in a statement shared with The Hacker News.

Dutch mobile security company ThreatFabric said it identified replacements for eight Indonesian banking apps, while credential targeting in the malware spans Indonesia, China, India, Mexico, Morocco and Thailand.

"For these, the RAT detects the installed banking app through accessibility, checks its signing certificate against a stored reference, [and] then shows a fake 'update' prompt," ThreatFabric explained.
"It opens Android's uninstaller for the genuine app without waiting for the user to tap, and downloads the bank-specific replacement in parallel."
The malware is delivered by shopping, adult video, and entertainment dropper apps that carry the trojan as a separate installation package, which is then served as an in-app update.

"Behind that content the dropper runs a fixed startup routine: it collects promotion-tracking data, fetches its campaign configuration, and checks whether the payload, the Hirudo RAT, is already installed with its accessibility service and notification access enabled."

extraction.body: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a new Android banking trojan called Hirudo that works by replacing legitimate banking apps with purpose-built patched versions designed to bypass security checks from inside the app itself, marking a new escalation in financial fraud. Dutch mobile security company ThreatFabric said it identified replacements for eight Indonesian banking apps, while credential targeting in the malware spans Indonesia, China, India, Mexico, Morocco and Thailand. "The operation combines credential theft, device takeover, screen and camera capture, and SMS theft, in combination with a fairly mature backend," Eward Driehuis, vice president of fraud engineering at ThreatFabric, said in a statement shared with The Hacker News. Hirudo facilitates on-device credential theft and live remote control. The malware is delivered by shopping, adult video, and entertainment dropper apps that carry the trojan as a separate installation package, which is then served as an in-app update. "The lure is functional, loading real content in a WebView, a storefront, a video catalogue or short dramas, so the experience looks legitimate," ThreatFabric explained. "Behind that content the dropper runs a fixed startup routine: it collects promotion-tracking data, fetches its campaign configuration, and checks whether the payload, the Hirudo RAT, is already installed with its accessibility service and notification access enabled." If it's not present, it displays a fake in-app update prompt to trigger the installation of the malware. It's worth emphasizing that Hirudo is installed as a second app and must be granted its own permissions before it can carry out the malicious activities. As observed in the case of StreamRat , the malware implements an anti-detection technique based on blocking Internet access by configuring a deliberately non-functional VPN connection prior to the payload installation. This is seen as an attempt to prevent other apps and services, like Google Play Protect, from carrying out cloud-based checks of the payload. "However, Play Protect also provides offline detection for known potentially harmful applications, meaning that the mechanism does not completely disable its protection," ThreatFabric noted last month. "We therefore assess that the technique is more likely intended to reduce the effectiveness of online reputation and code-analysis mechanisms rather than bypass Play Protect entirely." Depending on the nature of the lure app used, the dropper is also designed to serve bogus screens to capture payment PINs, serve fake screens requesting login credentials for banks and wallet apps, display fake lock screen pattern and PIN overlays, and facilitate total remote control of the device. While all this behavior is par for the course when it comes to Android banking trojans, it's their attempts to replace the target banking app with a tampered copy that stand out. Specifically, the purpose-built replacements embed a hooking engine to blind signature, accessibility, screen-capture, and Play Integrity checks from within the app. The replacement targets eight Indonesian apps. "For these, the RAT detects the installed banking app through accessibility, checks its signing certificate against a stored reference, [and] then shows a fake 'update' prompt," ThreatFabric explained. "It opens Android's uninstaller for the genuine app without waiting for the user to tap, and downloads the bank-specific replacement in parallel." While the need for having to remove the app before installing its near-identical malicious copy is a "real constraint," the mechanism offers the ability to bypass the banking app's own security checks by returning responses fed by the attacker beforehand. This involves returning the genuine app signing certificate, returning an empty list when querying for enabled accessibility services, and stripping the FLAG_SECURE flag so that the app's screens can be viewed and recorded remotely. "Key-attestation certificates are re-signed with a bundled keybox, and Play Integrity requests are relayed over plain HTTP to an operator-controlled server, which returns a verdict for the app to accept," the mobile security company said. "Two details are worth underlining for defenders. First, the attestation keybox the engine ships is not the operators' own: it is a publicly leaked keybox. Second, because the Integrity request is relayed rather than genuinely produced, a valid Integrity response alone is not evidence of an untampered app." Evidence indicates that the malware is distributed via fake web pages masquerading as Google Play Store landing pages for shopping, short drama, and football apps. Unsuspecting users are assessed to be directed to these websites through ads on Meta-owned social media platforms. The entire operation rests on a backend that combines device control with the ability to manage different campaigns and stolen data, including device records, lock-screen history, and financial profiles containing monthly income and risk-score fields. "Hirudo marks a deliberate escalation in how Android bankers approach hardened applications," ThreatFabric said. "By moving its tampering inside the target app, the operation shifts the contest from the device to the application's own integrity checks, and from a bespoke patch to a reusable engine that can be retargeted at other apps and regions." "Once an app can be replaced, its locally produced signals, signature, accessibility list, and integrity verdict, must be treated as attacker-influenced and verified server-side," ThreatFabric said. Last month, the findings came a little over a month after the cybersecurity firm revealed StreamRat's targeting of Spanish-speaking users via Meta and TikTok advertisements impersonating a free TV streaming service named Streamtv Esp to enable control over compromised Android devices. "StreamRat abuses accessibility services and MediaProjection to provide operators with near-complete control over infected devices, combining VNC and hidden-screen control, UI-tree collection, keylogging, credential-stealing overlays, internet and screen-blocking capabilities," ThreatFabric said. Evidence indicates that the malware is distributed via fake web pages masquerading as Google Play Store landing pages for shopping, short drama, and football apps. Unsuspecting users are assessed to be directed to these websites through ads on Meta-owned social media platforms.

The entire operation rests on a backend that combines device control with the ability to manage different campaigns and stolen data, including device records, lock-screen history, and financial profiles containing monthly income and risk-score fields.

"Hirudo marks a deliberate escalation in how Android bankers approach hardened applications," ThreatFabric said. "By moving its tampering inside the target app, the operation shifts the contest from the device to the application's own integrity checks, and from a bespoke patch to a reusable engine that can be retargeted at other apps and regions."
"Once an app can be replaced, its locally produced signals, signature, accessibility list, and integrity verdict, must be treated as attacker-influenced and verified server-side," ThreatFabric said.

Last month, the findings came a little over a month after the cybersecurity firm revealed StreamRat's targeting of Spanish-speaking users via Meta and TikTok advertisements impersonating a free TV streaming service named Streamtv Esp to enable control over compromised Android devices.

extraction.body: How to remove a Trojan, Virus, Worm, or other Malware A new Android malware called Hirudo steals bank account credentials by replacing legitimate banking apps with modified versions that disable security checks. Researchers identified malicious copies of eight banking apps that use a hooking engine to bypass app-signature, Accessibility, and Play Integrity checks by substituting certificate information or returning empty lists. Threat actors can use Hirudo to steal credentials, remotely control infected phones in real time, collect messages, capture screenshots, and record audio. A report today from mobile security company ThreatFabric notes that Hirudo has been observed impersonating at least seven Indonesian banks, but the malware also targets financial organizations in China, India, Mexico, Morocco, and Thailand. The malware is typically delivered via apps for shopping (Shopora), adult content (1V1 X), or short drama (ZoyaTV, KoiShort) that appear legitimate and provide the promised functionality. The researchers say that these apps act as malware loaders for Hirudo, showing a fake “update” notification that leads to permission-granting prompts, including for Accessibility services Once installed, Hirudo launches the real banking app’s uninstaller, downloads a patched copy, and abuses its Accessibility permission to install it. ThreatFabric explains that this is a delicate, risky process for the malware, since the victim can interrupt it at two points. ThreatFabric found that the malicious copy of a banking app retains almost all of the original app’s code, but loads a hooking engine built on the open-source frameworks YAHFA and Dobby. When launched, the patched app performs the following evasion actions: “With the engine running inside the banking app's own process, the app's defenses are turned against it,” the researchers say . However, ThreatFabric explains there are certain limitations to these evasion methods. The bundled attestation keybox has been publicly leaked, and Google lists two of its certificates as compromised, so server-side revocation checks can detect those forgeries. Once active on the device, Hirudo can steal banking passwords, payment PINs, device-unlock secrets, and SMS messages, stream the screen to operators, and provide access to both cameras. The malware’s fake checkout pages collect payment PINs, then display a fabricated payment-success result to deceive victims while it steals data. ThreatFabric found that Hirudo currently targets Indonesian banking apps and found thousands of application-credential entries in an unsecured backend panel, along with device, lock-screen, and financial-profile data. However, the victim count remains unknown. According to the researchers, “Hirudo marks a deliberate escalation in how Android bankers approach hardened applications,” shifting the focus from device-level integrity checks to the security mechanisms built into banking apps. The researchers suggest that banks should validate integrity and attestation server-side, bind checks to sessions and protected actions, and retain behavioral and transaction-risk controls. Android users are strongly recommended to keep their devices up-to-date, avoid installing APK files sourced from unofficial Android stores, and periodically run Play Protect scans. While all this behavior is par for the course when it comes to Android banking trojans, it's their attempts to replace the target banking app with a tampered copy that stand out.
"Hirudo marks a deliberate escalation in how Android bankers approach hardened applications," ThreatFabric said.

"By moving its tampering inside the target app, the operation shifts the contest from the device to the application's own integrity checks, and from a bespoke patch to a reusable engine that can be retargeted at other apps and regions."

"The operation combines credential theft, device takeover, screen and camera capture, and SMS theft, in combination with a fairly mature backend," Eward Driehuis, vice president of fraud engineering at ThreatFabric, said in a statement shared with The Hacker News.

Dutch mobile security company ThreatFabric said it identified replacements for eight Indonesian banking apps, while credential targeting in the malware spans Indonesia, China, India, Mexico, Morocco and Thailand.

"For these, the RAT detects the installed banking app through accessibility, checks its signing certificate against a stored reference, [and] then shows a fake 'update' prompt," ThreatFabric explained.
"It opens Android's uninstaller for the genuine app without waiting for the user to tap, and downloads the bank-specific replacement in parallel."
The malware is delivered by shopping, adult video, and entertainment dropper apps that carry the trojan as a separate installation package, which is then served as an in-app update.

"Behind that content the dropper runs a fixed startup routine: it collects promotion-tracking data, fetches its campaign configuration, and checks whether the payload, the Hirudo RAT, is already installed with its accessibility service and notification access enabled."
